ai.description: This slender snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown or black with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a blunt, shield-like tail ending in a small, bicarinate scale. It belongs to Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis woodmasoni* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, sharp, upward-curving keel on its terminal tail shield, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis woodmasoni* inhabits the high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Woodmason's earth snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis woodmasoni* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis woodmasoni* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests above 1,000 meters.
